name: Place Pulse 2.0: Six Urban Perceptions (16 cities)
description:
Method replication: same six questions and pairwise design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of 16 cities, © Google). Dubey, Naik, Parikh, Raskar & Hidalgo (2016, "Deep Learning the City", ECCV 2016, LNCS) introduced the Place Pulse 2.0 dataset: 110,988 images from 56 cities and 1.17 million pairwise comparisons from 81,630 online volunteers on six attributes (safe, lively, boring, wealthy, depressing, beautiful). A Siamese-like convolutional network trained with joint classification and ranking losses predicted the human pairwise judgements.

What participants do: after consent, 5 pairs for each of six questions: which place looks safer, livelier, more beautiful, wealthier, more depressing, more boring. Images are drawn at random from 190 views of 16 cities on six continents (New York, Boston, Toronto, Mexico City, São Paulo, Santiago, London, Paris, Amsterdam, Stockholm, Linz, Salzburg, Bucharest, Johannesburg, Tokyo, Sydney). Then age, gender and where they grew up.

Analysis as in the paper: per-image scores for each attribute from pairwise wins (the paper's Q-score / TrueSkill), compared across cities, and used as labels for a pairwise ranking model.

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are new Google Street View views (2016–2026) of 16 of the 56 cities, 10–14 per city; (2) the original website allowed unlimited votes; this template asks 5 pairs per attribute. The earlier version of this template showed 62 photographs cropped from the paper PDF.
